newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wall Street wallops Australian stocks at open.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street wallops Australian stocks at open.

text.p: The Australian share market slid lower at the open on Friday after Wall Street slumped to its biggest loss in six weeks after strong economic data saw fears of a U.S. Fed interest rate tightening fears re-emerge.
Turnover was at high levels as exercises of August series options were put through the market after Thursday's expiry.
At the opening, the All Ordinaries index slid 14.80 points to 2264.5. September share index futures dived 16 points to 2263, a 1.5 point discount to the index.
Traders said that with U.S. long bond yields hurdling the seven percent barrier, local markets had played followed the leader.
"Overseas markets are setting the pace today," said a Sydney-based dealer.
"The seven percent (yield) level spooks investors and that has flowed through to here."
Players saw little chance of much change over the day with local attention focussed on profits due later today.
A feature early was Anaconda Nickel whose shares slid after saying late on Thursday that it would restart a legal action after earlier saying it had been discontinued.
"They have dropped. They can't seem to work out how to handle the legal challenge," the dealer said.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about 10 to four, while about 41 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
